source_title: IMF Aging Economies and AI Adoption
direct_observation: Old-age dependency is positively associated with process AI or automation adoption; a ten-point increase raises adoption probability by about 0.6 percentage points after controls, with stronger effects among large firms and developing-country groups
missing_stage: substitution job quality care capacity older-person wellbeing and local service access
evidence_status: official firm-level study with IV and survey limitations
next_test: follow named firms and workers through capital adoption tasks staffing and service outcomes

source_title: IMF process and product AI channels
direct_observation: Aging predicts both process adoption and AI product development; only 82 firms overlap and product adoption is present across services and manufacturing
missing_stage: named product or service user affordability care quality worker transition and social outcome
next_test: compare process adopter product adopter non-adopter and user outcomes

unit_or_scope: formal private firms in aging economies
direct_observation: The study tests workforce skill gaps and labor regulations as firm-reported obstacles, linking demographic structure to perceived operational constraint
missing_stage: technology solution versus burden shift to workers caregivers and users
next_test: join labor-constraint report to adoption investment training and worker/user outcome

direct_observation: AI may raise productivity and alleviate labor shortages in aging societies subject to adoption and complementary capabilities
missing_stage: implementation accessibility trust agency distribution and care/service outcomes
next_test: trace adoption to older-user and worker encounter

direct_observation: Firm AI adoption can rise rapidly while sophisticated use remains shallow and concentrated; local adaptation and scale are required for gains
missing_stage: small-firm uptake local language care/service use workforce transition and outcomes
next_test: compare firm size and region on depth skills use and downstream outcome

unit_or_scope: older workers and aging workforces in OECD
direct_observation: Aging raises concerns about older-worker employability wellbeing innovation and productivity and may turn a demographic dividend into a deficit
missing_stage: AI-enabled retention discrimination training care burden and intergenerational distribution
next_test: follow older workers through training redesign retention and wellbeing with non-adopter comparator
